title: Nevada Museum of Art presents a live seismic earthwork by Ken Goldberg
summary: The Nevada Museum of Art presents ReBloom: Reno, a new site-specific earthwork by Bay Area artist Ken Goldberg, created in collaboration with Kabir Shah, Sanjay Krishnan, Fernanda Viégas, and Martin Wattenberg. On view October 10, 2026 through February 7, 2027 in the Thomas Lee Bottom Gallery, the installation draws on live seismic data from a local seismometer station, transforming the earth's constant motion into circular blooms of color that suggest fields of flowers. “As an artist and roboticist, I use new technologies to express the contrasts between what is natural and what is artificial, the liminal spaces between reality and representation. I’m excited to present this installation created uniquely for the Nevada Museum of Art,” said Ken Goldberg. title: Bertoia's Oct. 23 Collectors Sale introduces historic militaria alongside vintage toys
summary: For the first time ever – on Friday, October 23rd – Bertoia’s will auction a selection of historic militaria, featuring primarily World War II material with the addition of select World War I items. The Collectors Sale includes American, German, British, Italian and other European artifacts, with helmets and headgear, field equipment and instruments, badges and insignia, banners, personal effects and more. Complementing the militaria is an appealing selection of period toy soldiers and automobiles, along with a wonderful assortment of Japanese tin robots and space toys. In all, 425 rare and highly collectible lots will cross the auction block. Bertoia Auctions extends a special thank you to militaria consultant Joel Bohy for sharing his knowledge and expertise in the research and cataloging of this collection.

title: Fine jewelry from New York private collection featured at Roland's October 17th auction
summary: Roland Auctions NY will feature an important collection of jewelry and signature pieces from a Water Mill, NY private collection on October 17th, 2026 at 10am, also offering hundreds of lots of Fine Art & Sculpture, Decorative Art, 20th-Century Modern, Antique & Vintage Furniture, Textiles, Silver, Furs and Couture, Rugs, Collectibles and Asia. Previews for the September 19th auction will be held on Thursday, October 15th and Friday, October 16th from 10am until 6pm. Fine jewelry highlights from this Water Mill, NY collection being offered at Roland Auctions will include pieces by Tiffany, Angela Cummings, Jean Schlumberger, Bulgari, Gurhan 24 K gold items, Buccellati, Mauboussin, and Cartier, with a Patek Philippe 18K yellow gold and diamond Collection 4 Wristwatch with brown dial, integrated gold band, diamond accents and quartz movement, dial, case

title: The Gallery at The Watermark at Brooklyn Heights presents 'Julie A. Gross: Color as Spirit '
summary: Color as Spirit, a retrospective of work by Julie A. Gross , is on view in The Gallery at The Watermark in Brooklyn Heights through January 3, 2027. Curated by Patricia Vinyard, the exhibition features paintings, sculptures, and works on paper from when Julie began her professional art career in the 1970s through 2023. Located at 21 Clark Street, the gallery is open daily from 9:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. The 56 pieces in the exhibition range in size from intimate sculptural works of Julie’s 1970s Body Tracing series to large paintings such as Half Paynes, which measures 90 inches wide. Julie used a variety of painting and drawing mediums and surfaces, applying newly learned principles in each successive series, and several of these series and materials are included in the show. title: Cleveland Museum of Art presents major international survey of Goryeo dynasty sacred art
summary: Ten Kings of Hell: The Afterlife in Medieval Korea, a landmark international exhibition, explores the artistic legacy of the Goryeo dynasty (918–1392) in relation to their beliefs about death and the afterlife in Korea. Organized in partnership with the National Museum of Korea, the exhibition presents an exceptional array of important artworks, including Korea’s national treasure and the CMA’s recent acquisitions—the Fourth King of Hell from the late 1300s, the Knife Sheath from the 1100s (Apollo’s Acquisition of the Year Award 2022), and the Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva from the 1300s, as well as a newly rediscovered Goryeo-period

title: Artemis Fine Arts spans cultures and centuries in October auction
summary: Artemis Fine Arts will bring together Native American art, Pre-Columbian antiquities, African and Oceanic sculpture, Asian devotional objects and works from the ancient Mediterranean in its " Native American | Ethnographic | Ancient Art " auction on October 14. The wide-ranging sale reflects the Colorado auction house's specialty in objects that cross traditional collecting categories, moving from archaeological material and tribal art to Asian sculpture, textiles, jewelry and historical artifacts. title: Iconic works by Minor White, Aaron Siskind and Harry Callahan on view at the High
summary: This fall, the High Museum of Art is the exclusive Southeast venue for “Photography as a Way of Life: Minor White, Aaron Siskind, and Harry Callahan” (Oct. 9, 2026-Feb. 7, 2027), a touring exhibition that examines the overlapping careers of these profoundly influential photographers, teachers and thinkers who redefined photography in the mid-20th century. Drawing from the rich holdings of the Princeton University Art Museum and its Minor White Archive, the exhibition features iconic and previously unpublished color and black-and-white prints, rarely seen slides, and an array of published and archival materials. “‘Photography as a Way of Life’

title: Kunstmuseum Brandts surveys four centuries of still life art in 'Still on the Table!'
summary: Beauty never goes out of fashion—and neither does our preoccupation with the fleeting nature of life and the decay of all living things. Now, Kunstmuseum Brandts presents a wealth of examples of a much-loved genre in art: the still life. Expect plenty of arrangements of fruit, candles, half-empty decanters and platters piled high. Still on the Table! opens at Kunstmuseum Brandts on 10 October 2026. Things are never just things. We surround ourselves with objects that hold particular significance for us, and we share photographs of everyday possessions online. Still lifes—carefully arranged compositions of objects—have fascinated artists for centuries. It is a much-loved genre that can accommodate both powerful emotions and quiet moments, extravagant living and poignant decay. Kunstmuseum Brandts now presents the genre through more than ninety works spanning over 400 years of art history, from the symbol-laden paintings of the seventeenth

title: The Met marks the 100th anniversary of Val-Kill Industries with exhibition
summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art presents Cottage Industry: The Val-Kill Furniture Shop, on view through May 9, 2027. Timed to the centennial anniversary of Val-Kill Industries, the exhibition offers a focused exploration of a trailblazing furniture workshop, founded in 1926, by Eleanor Roosevelt and fellow activists at their rural Hyde Park, New York, retreat. Bringing together over 40 works from The Met collection and key loans from the Val-Kill Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (National Park Service) and the Franklin D. Roosevelt Library, the presentation reveals how the workshop founders and artisans looked to historical collections at The Met for inspiration while developing a progressive craft community that would serve as a model for the Roosevelts’ later New Deal WPA programs. “Cottage Industry: The Val-Kill Furniture Shop offers a compelling perspective on

title: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam transforms 835 m² into dance floor for major 'DISCO' exhibition
summary: A floor of 835 m2 at Wereldmuseum Amsterdam has been transformed into one vast dance floor. With the exhibition DISCO, the museum pays an electrifying tribute to this hugely influential musical movement. Emerging from the underground clubs of New York, this iconic genre grew during the 1970s into a worldwide social revolution centred on freedom, inclusion, and self-expression. Visitors to the exhibition dance their way through hundreds of original disco tracks, videos, art, fashion, and design, experiencing the connective power of disco. DISCO is a large-scale exploration of an influential movement that extends far beyond music alone, for disco transformed the music industry, reshaped nightlife, and became a catalyst for emancipation. The exhibition presents disco as an interplay of social change, artistic innovation, and political struggle, placing the genre firmly within its historical and societal context. title: Pace London presents Kylie Manning's solo debut featuring Thames clay pigments
summary: Pace will present The Mudlarkers, an exhibition of new paintings by New York-based artist Kylie Manning, at its London gallery from October 13 through November 14. In these paintings, Manning embraces an intensity of color and compositional movement to create works held at the apex of a tide, where one state has not yet yielded to the next. Marking her first solo exhibition in London, The Mudlarkers represents a continuation of Manning’s ongoing practice of creating site-specific paintings attuned to the unique histories and atmospheres of their destinations. Here, she incorporates Hampshire and London clay, along with silt from the River Thames, into her pigments, drawing on the local tradition of mudlarking, which dates to the late eighteenth century. Scavenging the banks of the Thames at low tide, mudlarkers once searched for objects of value to sell; today, they seek the historical artifacts—Roman coins, pottery shards, tobacco pipes, and other centuries-old fragments

title: National Museum of American History commemorates 250 years of the gunboat Philadelphia
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History is the home of the gunboat Philadelphia, a rare surviving intact American revolutionary war fighting vessel that was part of a small American fleet. The Philadelphia sank on Lake Champlain during the Battle of Valcour Island 250 years ago Oct. 11, 1776, but the small fleet was successful in delaying the advancing British troops. The Philadelphia is currently undergoing a multi-year conservation treatment, on view to the public in the “The Gunboat Philadelphia Preservation Project” exhibition, and the museum will mark the 250th anniversary of the historic battle with updates about the conservation treatment and new historical research into the boat’s construction and time afloat. title: Centro Botín hosts Solange Pessoa's first solo exhibition in Spain
summary: Of Day or Night is the first exhibition in Spain dedicated to Solange Pessoa (Ferros, Brazil, 1961), an artist internationally recognized for her multidisciplinary practice, encompassing sculpture, painting, video, performance, installation, and drawing. Her work explores themes connected to nature, memory, the body, spirituality, and the cycles of life, weaving together a range of local references such as Brazilian modernism, colonial Baroque, and Indigenous cosmologies with influences from Land Art, Arte Povera, Surrealism, and prehistoric symbolism. Her work has deep roots in the landscape and context of Minas Gerais, a region of extraordinary natural wealth that has historically been one of Brazil’s key mining centers. Through the use of organic and mineral materials, Pessoa establishes a direct relationship with this land and culture, evoking processes of metamorphosis and an oneiric engagement with landscape and matter. title: Smithsonian Women's Committee awards its 60th-Anniversary Grant to "Lights Out: Recovering the Night Sky" project
summary: The Smithsonian Women’s Committee (SWC) has awarded its 60th Anniversary Special Grant to the Smithsonian Institution Traveling Exhibition Service | Smithsonian Affiliations (SITES | Affiliations) for the project “Lights Out: Recovering the Night Sky.” This year, SWC celebrates 60 years of fundraising and philanthropy on behalf of the Smithsonian Institution. For six decades, SWC has raised more than $15 million to make thoughtful, high-impact and lasting grants and gifts across Smithsonian museums, research facilities and the National Zoo and Smithsonian Conservation Biology Institute. title: Pangolin London brings together six decades of postwar sculpture in "Modern Sculptors"
summary: Pangolin London is presenting Modern Sculptors, an exhibition bringing together important works by artists who helped shape the development of British and European sculpture from the mid-twentieth century onward. On view in the gallery’s main space through October 31, 2026, the exhibition spans more than six decades and traces a period of intense experimentation in which sculptors moved away from established monument traditions, embraced abstraction, and explored new possibilities in both ancient and industrial materials. At the center of the exhibition is a generation shaped by the social, political and cultural upheavals of the Second World War and its aftermath. title: Lumo Art & Tech Festival in Oulu presents its full programme featuring Björk
summary: As part of the Oulu2026 European Capital of Culture year, the new ten-day festival features a rich programme of professional and public events, bringing art together with technology and science through immersive exhibitions, light and sound art, performances, talks and seminars across the city Opening on 13 November. Björk will bring three audiovisual installations to Oulu, following their debut in Reykjavík: Ancestress, Sorrowful Soil and Björk Orkestral. The programme also features exhibitions by international artists and institutions including Jakob Kudsk Steensen, Josefina Nelimarkka and Fotografiska Tallinn. title: Reflex Amsterdam presents Enoc Perez's 'Selected Drawings & Paintings'
summary: Reflex Amsterdam is presenting Selected Drawings & Paintings, an exhibition bringing together works by Enoc Perez that move through memory, modernism, desire and the unstable space between abstraction and representation. “I’m just trying to steal a time that preceded me,” Perez has said. “A moment when everything was new to me and when possibility was realistic.” That sense of reaching towards something just out of reach runs throughout the exhibition. Perez’s paintings draw from the visual language of modernism, architecture and popular imagery, yet his subjects are never simply descriptions of what they depict. They become carriers of memory; personal, collective and imagined. The hotels of Puerto Rico, in particular, return as places suspended between lived experience and projection. title: Vera List Center presents Brazilian artist Rosana Paulino in '¿História Natural?'
summary: The Vera List Center for Art and Politics is presenting Rosana Paulino: ¿História Natural?, an exhibition celebrating the groundbreaking work of Brazilian artist Rosana Paulino, recipient of the 2025–2027 Jane Lombard Prize for Art and Social Justice. Inaugurated as part of the VLC Forum 2026: Matter of Intelligence, the exhibition is presented at The New School at the Arnold and Sheila Aronson Galleries, Parsons School of Design, from October 9 through November 1, 2026. Anchored by her landmark artist book ¿História Natural?, the exhibition traces Rosana Paulino’s critical examinations of the entanglements between science, race, knowledge, and power. title: M Leuven explores 16th-century artistic exchange between Italy and Low Countries
summary: M, for the first time, highlights the artistic exchange between Italy and the Low Countries in the 16th century. Featuring masterpieces from renowned international museums, the exhibition tells the fascinating story of mutual influence, virtuoso craftsmanship, and a drive for innovation. Sculptures, paintings, drawings and prints reveal how artists from the Low Countries, who worked in Italy, left their mark on the visual language of the Renaissance. “The ‘Scultori Fiamminghi’ exhibition shows how movement, exchange and international networks drove art and culture forward – a story that resonates today more than ever.”– Bert Cornillie, Alderman for Culture and Chair of the board of directors of M Leuven In the early 16th century, pioneers such as Jan Gossaert, Pieter Coecke van Aelst and Cornelis Floris introduced the Italian Renaissance

title: Exhibition explores the enduring spirit of traditional aesthetics through a contemporary lens
summary: The Hong Kong Palace Museum and the Palace Museum jointly present a new thematic exhibition, “Design for the Forbidden City: Imperial Workshops of the Qing Court” (“Design for the Forbidden City”), in Gallery 5 of the HKPM. Featuring 157 treasures from the Palace Museum collection, including 14 grade-one national treasures, the exhibition celebrates the artistic ingenuity and superb craftsmanship of the Qing dynasty (1644–1911). Through the lens of contemporary design, the exhibition offers rare and insightful perspectives on the operation and aesthetic codes of the Qing Imperial Workshops. Seamlessly bridging past and present, the exhibition embodies the Museum’s core vision of bringing history and cultural heritage vividly to life. By inviting Hong Kong designers and other creative talents to participate in the exhibition design, the exhibition

title: Frida Orupabo brings first solo exhibition in Denmark to Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
summary: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg is presenting the first solo exhibition in Denmark by internationally acclaimed Norwegian-Nigerian artist Frida Orupabo, bringing together new collage works in the artist’s largest installation to date. Titled Get close enough and you can’t see, the exhibition opens October 8, 2026 and runs through May 9, 2027. Created specifically for Kunsten’s Alvar Aalto-designed building, the presentation unfolds through a labyrinthine exhibition architecture that places visitors physically among Orupabo’s works and complicates the usual relationship between viewer and image. Orupabo’s practice draws on a wide range of visual sources, including colonial archives, vintage pornography, cartoons, retro horror films and imagery found in obscure corners of the internet. title: Rijksmuseum unveils Kadir van Lohuizen's 'New Energy' photographic commission
summary: Document Netherlands is the Rijksmuseum’s annual photographic commission, which this year takes new energy as its subject. In nine panoramic photographs and a video installation, photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen shows how the North Sea and surrounding countries are changing at breakneck speed as a result of the rising demand for energy. New Energy explores places which largely remain beyond our view, such as an offshore wind farm under construction and the server room of a hermetically sealed data centre. The exhibition runs from 9 October 2026 to 17 January 2027. "I really had no idea of the scale and complexity of what is taking place behind the scenes around wind and solar energy, hydrogen, CO₂ storage, hydropower and data centres. title: Stephan Vanfleteren explores five-year marine obsession at Scheepvaartmuseum
summary: In Transcripts of a Sea, photographer Stephan Vanfleteren shares the enchantment that has literally driven him out to sea over the past five years. With a dangerous obsession and palpable longing, Stephan Vanfleteren analyses the sea in all its forms and lighting conditions. Along the coastline from northern France to the southern Netherlands, he sought out places where waves and swells manifest themselves as unpredictable wonders. The photography exhibition Stephan Vanfleteren – Transcripts of a Sea is a quest into the depths of a surface and a small still life of a vast, living sea. Through surprising images, Vanfleteren reveals its diverse forms: from smooth water surfaces, ephemeral misty scenes and storm-like threats to a devastatingly stormy or, conversely, deceptively calm sea. “Whilst the world is on fire, I head for the shore. title: Four decades of California Arts & Crafts masterworks headline sale
summary: On October 16, Rago and Toomey & Co. present The Goldstein Family Collection, an exceptional range of important and rare Arts & Crafts furniture, lighting, and decorative objects, in tandem with complementary fine art. Emphasizing the movement's distinctive expression in Southern California, this collection assembled over four decades features masterworks by Greene & Greene, Dirk van Erp, Elizabeth Eaton Burton, Arthur and Lucia Mathews, Gustav Stickley, Tiffany Studios, Grueby Faience Company, Frederick Hurten Rhead, Albert R. Valentien, C.F.A. Voysey, Gustave Baumann, and several others. The preeminent highlight is a dramatic, circa-1904 Greene & Greene pairing consisting of a library table and lamp from the Adelaide Tichenor House in Long Beach (est. $100,000–150,000).
